panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Implied 11.7% is roughly fair, marginally rich. Realised mean abs is 8.57% / median 7.53%, but the Q4 print is UNFI's fattest-tailed event of the year because it carries initial full-year guidance -- the +18.45% outlier in the sample is exactly last year's Q4. I would centre the distribution at ~9-10% with a fat left tail.
key_drivers: Street sits above the company's own implied Q4 bar: FY26 guide implies Q4 adj EPS mid $0.55 while consensus is $0.62 -- near the top of the implied range, with the consensus mark unchanged over 30 days and Earnings ESP 0.00%.

The metric this trades on is not EPS -- it is net sales trajectory and the initial FY2027 guide. Q3 was a profit story and the stock still fell ~10% purely on a revenue miss. Market needs Q4 net sales at or above ~$7.7B and an FY27 frame consistent with a return to low-single-digit sales growth.

Offsetting: the comp is artificially easy (Q4 FY25 was cyber-hit), leverage is heading to ~2.3x, FCF guided ~$330M, and last year's equivalent Q4 print produced +18.45% even on a deliberately low initial FY26 guide.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: UNFI opens FY27 with its usual lowball wide range and the market discounts it exactly as it did in October 2025 -- a cyber-comp-flattered Q4, leverage improving, FCF confirmation and a reiterated FY28 EBITDA target can re-rate a high-operating-leverage equity hard off a base already 23% below its 52-week high.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source 60/90-day revision breadth or an explicit FY27 EBITDA consensus dollar figure; the FY27 anchor is snippet_only.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Sep-18 straddle prices ~11.7% event-day, ~55% above the 7.53% median and ~36% above the 8.57% mean of the last six realised prints. My view is a realistic modal ±7-9%. The reaction is over-priced, not under-priced -- I would not pay this straddle.
key_drivers: Skew and OI disagree: ATM puts bid richer than calls, yet Sep-18 OI is call-heavy (~3,500 calls vs ~1,200 puts) with the largest single-strike stack at the 45 call, 2.4% above spot. Hedgers pay up for downside while longs own cheap upside -- the pain trade is up.

De-risked tape, not a crowded long: stock fell ~9% into the print, near the bottom of its 90-day range and 23% off the 52-week high, while sell-side sits above spot (avg PT $49.38). Two of the last three prints were double-digit down moves, which conditions pre-emptive selling -- fuel for a gap up.

Modest but real squeeze ammo: 4.48% of float short, 5.3 days-to-cover, short interest rose +5.25% at the last settlement -- but that settlement is now stale and blind to the entire slide since. Front-month OI is thin, so dealer gamma is immaterial; do not expect pinning.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The June 9 print is the template that kills this: adjusted EBITDA +17% and EPS +75% y/y, and the stock still fell 10.3% because net sales missed and Conventional segment sales fell double digits. If the FY27 revenue guide again frames shrinkage as strategy, positioning will not save it.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source borrow fee/utilisation, IV rank/percentile, live put/call volume ratio, or dealer gamma positioning; short interest is stale (last settlement 24 days prior).

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: I expect ~7-9% absolute, below the 11.7% implied. The straddle is pricing above every realised print in the last six except the +18.45% outlier -- the event move looks over-priced rather than under-priced -- but the fat tail is real because this print carries the first FY27 guide.
key_drivers: Sentiment has decayed hard over 30 days: stock -10% on the month, broke its 50-DMA, consensus rating drifted to Hold, and consensus EPS has sat unchanged for 30 days -- no positive revision momentum, just apathy.

The narrative is fragile because it is a pure guidance story delivered by strangers: a CFO who started four weeks ago and a President/COO effective one month ago are delivering the first FY27 guide -- textbook reset/kitchen-sink conditions. Retail's other heuristic, average EPS surprise, has been worthless: the last two prints beat-and-faded.

Genuinely uncrowded, not a consensus long or short: short float only ~4.2-4.5% of float and falling, borrow low. No meme or pump signature at all. No squeeze fuel on a weak print, but also caps how much downside is genuinely 'positioned for'.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The bearish trade is already largely on. A stock pre-de-rated into the print with defensive options posture is the classic relief-rally setup: an in-line quarter plus a credible FY27 return-to-growth guide unwinds that hedge stack into a gap up -- the +18.45% print in this stock's own history is exactly that scenario.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: StockTwits sentiment/message-volume returned N/A and no Reddit/X thread volume was findable, so the sentiment read leans on price momentum, short-interest trend, and analyst/media tone as proxies rather than direct social data.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Base-rate absolute move ~9-12%, centred near 10%. Last-6 mean abs 8.57% (implied looks rich), but last-8 mean abs ~10.7% and the three sourced fiscal-Q4 prints averaged ~15% abs and all exceeded 11.7%. The implied is roughly fairly priced, not obviously rich, for the year-end guidance print.
key_drivers: Directional tilt is down but weak: 11 sourced quarters show 4 up / 7 down = 36% up; shrunk toward a neutral prior this is ~43-46% up, barely distinguishable from a coin flip.

Strong right-skew in the tails, n=8 recent: every move that broke the implied did so to the upside, while downside moves have clustered in a smaller band. Lower probability of up, larger magnitude when up -- direction and expected value point opposite ways.
Fiscal-Q4 seasonal cuts against the full-sample tilt (2 of 3 up) but n=3 and is not usable; no run-up into this print, so there is little momentum to unwind.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The one print each year that carries initial full-year guidance is exactly the print where UNFI has twice squeezed double digits; a credible FY27 EBITDA/EPS frame would blow through the 11.7% implied to the upside and the full-sample down tilt is thin enough to offer almost no protection.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Full historical reaction tables are paywalled, so pre-2025 magnitudes are reconstructed from news snippets; could not source current short interest or a multi-quarter post-earnings drift series independently.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Implied 11.7% is roughly fair, marginally rich. My realised estimate is ~8-11% absolute, skewed down -- justified by the initial FY27 guide from brand-new finance leadership, which resets guidance conservatively far more often than aggressively.
key_drivers: Diesel is the binding cross-asset variable and it has gone the wrong way since UNFI last guided: national retail diesel up sharply month-over-month on a Hormuz blockade with Brent elevated. Management explicitly named fuel/transportation pressure on the last call, and that model is now stale.

The customer channel is deteriorating, and peer prints have quantified it: Albertsons cut FY guidance sharply on softer industry unit trends and fell over 20% that day; Sprouts and Grocery Outlet both ran negative comps. Soft grocery units plus heavier promo squeezes a wholesaler's volume and price/mix.

Food distribution has been sold on this season's prints even when numbers were fine (Performance Food Group fell despite raising FY27 guidance). Offsetting: Russell 2000 is having a strong year and two beaten-down small-cap grocery peers that cleared a low bar were rewarded hard -- the regime is a tiebreaker, not a dominant force, since the event day itself is macro-clean.
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The bar is low enough that the peers who beat down and cleared it were rewarded, not punished. UNFI has beaten on profitability repeatedly and leverage is the lowest since FY2018. If FY27 EBITDA is guided to growth with fuel explicitly bridged, the same 'sales down, profits up, deleveraging' story the market sold in June gets bought in September.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source UNFI's current diesel hedge ratio or fuel-surcharge pass-through lag, a confirmed current short-interest-as-%-of-float figure, or UNFI's index-rebalance status.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: Implied 11.7% sits above both the historical mean (8.57%) and median (7.53%), so the straddle is modestly rich versus central tendency. But this is the FY27-initial-guidance print delivered by a CFO four weeks into the job -- precisely the configuration that produced the sample's largest moves. I mark fair at ~9-10%: magnitude is roughly priced, direction is not priced at all.
panel_verdicts.consensus_view_as_i_read_it: Mildly bullish. Prior-year Q4 was the cyberattack quarter, so consensus EPS is a near-cosmetic YoY jump against a broken comp; analysts are Buy with a target well above spot; leverage is the lowest since FY2018 on healthy FCF. The plain expectation is a profit beat plus a first FY27 guide confirming a return to growth, re-rating the stock back up.
panel_verdicts.strongest_reversal_case: On 9 June 2026 UNFI printed adjusted EBITDA +16.6% and EPS +75% YoY and the stock still closed -10.28%, because net sales missed and management merely narrowed FY26 ranges around unchanged midpoints -- this name does not get paid for profit quality when the top line and the guide disappoint. Layer on the guidance-reset mechanic: a brand-new CFO's first full-year guide is the single most reliable venue for a conservative bar, and management's own long-term algorithm implies FY27 EBITDA below the bull case circulating in retail commentary.
panel_verdicts.what_would_break_my_reversal_case: FY27 guidance at or above the algorithm's high end with wholesale sales guided back to growth, paired with a refreshed or enlarged buyback -- against a stock already well off its highs, that flips into a squeeze.
key_drivers: FY27 initial guide is the whole event; company algorithm implies EBITDA below the circulating bull case
New CFO four weeks in -- maximum incentive to set a low first-year bar; June precedent shows profit beats do not save this stock
Offsetting: run-in is negative not euphoric, meaningful short interest, and an aging buyback authorization due to lapse makes a refreshed repurchase a real same-day relief catalyst
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: The bearish setup is already partly expressed -- the stock fell into this print rather than ran up, so a merely adequate FY27 guide plus a new repurchase authorisation at a high FCF yield could produce the upside tail rather than the downside one.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source a genuine sell-side FY27 consensus for EBITDA/EPS -- the bull-case figure is a single author's estimate reached via search snippet only, which is the weakest link in the case.

panel_verdicts.expected_move_view: 11.7% implied vs 8.57% mean-abs / 7.53% median-abs realised. Implied sits above realised average, but this is the fiscal-Q4 guidance-setting print delivered by a CFO four weeks into the job -- the one slot where the fat tail is earned. I read fair value at roughly 9-12%, so the straddle is close to correctly priced with no edge in buying or selling vol; the skew, not the magnitude, is where the mispricing sits.
panel_verdicts.insider_signal: Near-null. Very few Form 4s in all of 2026 and zero transactions filed in the run-up to the print. The one discretionary open-market sale is fully explained by an announced executive departure, not a Q4 tell. The only genuine insider buy is eight months stale and well below spot. No 10b5-1 adoptions found, no cluster in either direction.
panel_verdicts.communication_signal: The real content is the leadership churn: five officer changes in ~7 weeks straddling the fiscal year-end, including a new CFO who started nine days after the fiscal year closed and did not author the long-term guidance framework. Hedging language was already inserted at Q3 (accelerating investment spend, embedded fuel/transportation pressure), and FY26 ranges were narrowed with midpoints held after which the stock fell double digits. Offsetting this, filing cadence into the print is clean and quiet -- no pre-announcement, no debt event.
key_drivers: Incoming-CFO rebase setup: a new CFO issues the first FY27 guide on a quarter he did not run -- the highest-base-rate conservative-guide configuration
Insider track is genuinely empty: no transactions in the run-up to the print, no buying cluster, and the only discretionary sale is fully explained by an announced departure
Alt-data corroboration of the Q3 spend hedge: a warehouse closure with layoffs phased entirely inside the reported quarter, plus modest short interest, so little squeeze fuel on a beat
panel_verdicts.top_risk_to_my_call: A new CFO's other classic first move is to buy credibility rather than sandbag -- reaffirming the long-term EBITDA target, announcing a buyback, or leaning on the deleveraging story. Consensus is only a modest EPS figure against a badly depressed prior-year comp, and this exact fiscal-Q4 slot produced the sample's single largest move to the upside.
panel_verdicts.evidence_note: Could not source current unusual-options prints, borrow-fee levels, or dark-pool data; no Google Trends, app-rank, web-traffic or Glassdoor series obtained. Alt-data is correlational: it confirms closure timing but says nothing about whether the cost sits inside guidance.

synthesis.move_band_note: unsigned magnitude band, right-skewed; the implied move is roughly one standard deviation, not a cap
synthesis.early_prediction: Panel is mildly bearish and genuinely mixed rather than falsely converged: six of seven land -6 to -25, but the options-positioning persona dissents at +12 on de-risked positioning and call-heavy open interest, keeping disparity at 24. The dominant theme across personas is the FY27 initial guide from a CFO four weeks into the job, against a historical mean print of only 8.57% but a fiscal-Q4/guidance-print history that produced the sample's largest move (+18.45%). Main caveat: reversal risk peaks at 68/100, the day's highest, on a case built around the same new-CFO catalyst the bear case rests on.
synthesis.red_team_survival_note: The red-team case (-12, reversal_risk 68, the panel's ceiling) is specific and sourced. It is directly answered, not left standing: the options-positioning persona (+12) reads the same new-leadership fact as a de-risked, sandbagged setup, from different evidence (options positioning and OI structure rather than fundamentals and history). That is a genuine disagreement about which way a single known catalyst cuts -- exactly the kind of dissent the panel exists to surface. Independence note: three of seven personas cited the same MarketBeat short-interest page and two cited the same June-drop recap article, but these are shared factual data points, not a shared narrative frame -- unlike ABM, no certainty override is warranted here.

independence_note: Seven isolated subagents; each received only the Phase-0 anchors (ticker, company, window, session, spot, implied move, historical realised moves) -- no dossier, no preliminary direction score, no other persona's verdict. One duplicate sentiment-persona run occurred due to a launch-tracking slip during a concurrency-limited fan-out; the duplicate was discarded and only one of the two independent sentiment verdicts is included above.
